why: Edwidge Danticat discusses her new novel Dey in conversation with Nicole Dennis-Benn at the main branch.

name: Unleashed: Pets of the Performing Arts
why: Exhibition exploring the role of pets in theater, dance, opera, and film, on view through February 6, 2027.

name: Declaring America: 1776 and Beyond
why: Exhibition examining documents and artifacts surrounding the Declaration of Independence and its legacy, on view through January 10, 2027.

name: Martha Graham: The Mother of Psychological Dance
why: Exhibition tracing Martha Graham's revolutionary approach to modern dance through archival materials, on view through November 7, 2026.

name: The Star-Spangled Banner First Edition
why: Exhibition featuring a first-edition broadside printing of The Star-Spangled Banner, on view through August 31, 2026.

name: Summer Jazz: Chembo Corniel Quintet
why: Free outdoor jazz in the museum's sculpture garden with the Chembo Corniel Quintet, part of the summer jazz series.

name: dapperQ presents Legacy
why: dapperQ's Legacy fashion event celebrates LGBTQ+ sartorial history and community at the Brooklyn Museum.

name: Art History Happy Hour: Sculpting the Senses
why: Cocktail-hour art history talk exploring sculpture and sensory experience in the museum's collection.

name: 29th Annual Bus Festival
why: The Transit Museum's 29th annual Bus Festival brings vintage buses, a scavenger hunt, and a museum store pop-up to Brooklyn Bridge Park.

name: Woodstock: Three Days of Peace and Music — Film Screening
why: Director's Cut screening of the Oscar-winning Woodstock documentary, part of the Flower Power exhibition's Woodstock anniversary programming at NYBG.

name: Deep Dive: The R46s and the Museum, 1976–2026
why: Transit historian Andy Sparberg traces the 50-year history of the R46 fleet—now retiring—alongside the Transit Museum's founding and NYC Transit's turbulent 1970s.

name: Transit Walk: Downtown Brooklyn
why: Guided walk tracing Downtown Brooklyn's transit history from early ferry landings through trolley and elevated railways into the subway era, ending at the museum's historic Court Street Station.

name: Mining the Archives: The Transit Museum's First 50 Years (Virtual)
why: Celebrate the Transit Museum's 50th anniversary with a virtual look inside its archives, from the 1965 World's Fair origins to its home in a decommissioned subway station.

name: Transit Walk: Gowanus and Carroll Gardens
why: Walking tour of Gowanus and Carroll Gardens exploring how industrialization and transit shaped these historically distinctive Brooklyn neighborhoods.

name: Vinyl Nights Presents Return to '76
why: 50th anniversary fundraiser dance party in the museum, with disco on the mezzanine and funk/hip-hop on the platform, all powered by vinyl. Two drink tickets included.

name: Underground NYC: Subway 101
why: Expert Transit Museum guides lead a ride-along tour revealing subway secrets, architecture, art, and archival images hidden in plain sight across old and new stations.

name: Transit Walk: Art and Design Secrets of Penn Station and Moynihan Train Hall
why: Tour of Penn Station's hidden Beaux-Arts remnants and the new public artworks extending into Moynihan Train Hall, the latest addition to this storied transportation hub.

name: NYC in Transit Film Series at Film Forum
why: Weekly film series at Film Forum celebrating the Transit Museum's 50th anniversary, screening classic films where New York's subway, buses, and elevated trains play a starring role.

name: Another Wonderland: Abram Champanier's Alice Mural
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Rescued and restored New Deal-era mural cycle originally created for Gouverneur Hospital's children's ward (1938–40), reimagining Alice in Wonderland characters exploring 1930s NYC, presented with NYC Health + Hospitals.

name: Free Late-Night Summer Wednesdays at MCNY
venue: Museum of the City of New York
source: Museum of the City of New York
via: Museum of the City of New York
why: Free Wednesday admission extended to 9pm through September 2, with a pop-up cocktail bar from 5–9pm — a chance to explore MCNY's full slate of exhibitions including Another Wonderland and The Occupied City.

name: Arbrasson Workshop with Daniel Fishkin
why: Learn to build your own Arbrasson — a rare wooden friction idiophone from France — with a history demo, materials included. Led by PW Alumni Resident Daniel Fishkin.

name: Nat Geo Advance Screening: LION
price: Free (RSVP required, first come first served)
why: Free advance screening of Nat Geo's LION, a four-part doc by Jon Favreau and BBC's Mike Gunton following a lion cub's four-year journey to become king — free passes on a first-come, first-served basis.

name: Secret Parlor Jazz: Home-Cooked Tunes & BBQ Dinner on the Upper East Side
why: Intimate parlor jazz in a private Upper East Side home, with BBQ dinner included — an experience that captures a vanishing mode of musical gathering. Also Sept 20 and Sept 27.

name: Secret Parlor Jazz: Home-Cooked Tunes & BBQ Dinner on the Upper East Side
why: Intimate parlor jazz in a private Upper East Side home, with BBQ dinner included.

name: Harlem: The Renaissance, The Neighborhood, The Legacy — Walking Tour
why: Thought Gallery Curations guided walking tour of Harlem covering the original Swing Street, where Billie Holiday was discovered, and the local roots of the 1963 March on Washington. Led by a local expert.

name: PhDs & Pints: The Neuroscience of Shared Experience
why: Free PhDs & Pints session on interbrain synchrony — how music, rhythm, and altered states pull separate nervous systems into a shared rhythm — with live music and Q&A by psychedelic cognitive neuroscientist Isabel Bermudez.

name: Facts Machine: Burrows of NYC (Urban Ecology Trivia)
why: Three scientists-turned-pub-trivia-hosts bring their Facts Machine show to Caveat with an urban ecology theme — rats, burrows, and the hidden wildlife of NYC, filtered through science comedy.

name: Birthright (Off-Broadway)
venue: Robert W. Wilson MCC Theater Space
why: Jonathan Spector's new off-Broadway play follows six Jewish Millennial friends navigating two decades of identity, memory, and diverging views on Israel — runs through August 23. Recommended by Thought Gallery.

name: 2001: A Space Odyssey (70mm)
why: Kubrick's 70mm masterpiece on MoMI's big Redstone Theater screen — one of four August showings in the See It Big: 70mm series.

name: 2001: A Space Odyssey (70mm)
why: Kubrick's 70mm masterpiece on MoMI's big Redstone Theater screen — one of four August showings in the See It Big: 70mm series.

name: The Untouchables (70mm)
why: Brian De Palma's Mamet-scripted crime epic in 70mm, part of the See It Big: 70mm and De Palma: Summer of Suspense series at MoMI.

name: Botanical Illustration 1 — BBG Fall Class
why: Five-session course in graphite botanical illustration — draw plants from direct observation with an instructor. Good entry point for anyone who's wanted to draw plants accurately.

name: Fall Container Gardening — BBG Class
why: Evening workshop on building fall container gardens with ornamental grasses, asters, salvia, and coral bells — practical and hands-on.

name: Wild Seed Collection: Ethics and Practice — BBG Course
time: Saturday Oct 17 (BBG, 1–4 PM) + Sunday Oct 18 (field trip, 2–5 PM)
why: Two-session course (classroom + NYC field trip) on the ethics and practice of collecting wild seed — when seeds are ready, how to assess plant populations responsibly, and seasonal patterns.
